transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-09-10
- Time: 16:00 PST
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Brian Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (Tileridge Head of MLOps), Priya Narayanan (Platform Eng), Sam Ortiz (Security Lead), Leah Kim (PM)

Auto summary (from call): Kickoff oriented around private deployment (VPC), security needs (KMS, audit), and perf SLOs. Action items assigned and dry-run pilot planned.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya, I'll be your AE on this engagement, and Brian is our SE.
[00:12] Jordan: Hey, Jordan here, thanks. we've got Priya and Sam and Leah on the call — this is our infra and security delegation.
[00:20] Brian: hi team, i'll mostly cover the connectivity and perf stuff, and we'll try to keep the deep infra bits to the end so we don't run over.
[00:28] Leah: thanks, we put together a rough 8-week runway and wanted to validate assumptions.

[01:02] Maya: high level agenda — 1) what you're trying to achieve (success criteria), 2) infra constraints (VPC, private deployment), 3) security/compliance needs, 4) pilot scope and timeline. sound good?
[01:15] Priya: yep. the most important thing for us right now is predictable latency — our alerting pipeline needs sub-200ms median and p95 under 400ms for short prompts. also we have strict egress policies.
[01:32] Sam: and from security, we need SOC2-like audit events, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, and a retention policy for logs.

[02:10] Brian: ok that helps. quick clarification: when you say private deployment, are you expecting Redwood Private in a VPC peered model or an on-prem install?
[02:20] Jordan: initial go-live will be VPC (cloud) with peered connectivity into our Prod VPC. on prem is a later discussion.
[02:32] Maya: perfect. on the network side we typically see two patterns — peering with a priv-az route or customer-hosted NAT and proxy. we can do peering but need the CIDR and routing.
[02:45] Priya: we'll have to check overlapping CIDRs; our infra is pretty segmented. also egress is locked down so we'll need to open a few endpoints.

[03:10] Brian: got it. for throughput and latency, what's the expected QPS for the alerting use-case?
[03:18] Jordan: in steady state maybe 10 qps, spikes up to 60 for market bursts. each call is short, ~64 tokens on average.
[03:28] Brian: that's helpful. we usually recommend a small dedicated pool for low-latency workload and enable prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts. note: caching helps percentile latency but not first-token.

[04:05] Sam: quick question on KMS — we need to ensure keys never leave our KMS and that Redwood can sign/encrypt with CMK. do you support HSM-backed keys?
[04:18] Maya: yes, we have integrations with major KMS providers and support customer-managed keys; in previous deployments we've routed encryption at rest through the customer's KMS.
[04:29] Elena: small note, sometimes in our docs it's called Redwood Privat or Redwood Dedicaed in notes — ignore that — but the capability is what matters.

[05:02] Priya: on audit logs, we need event granularity down to request-level traces for 90 days. is that supported?
[05:12] Brian: yes we can stream audit events to your logging endpoint (S3/CloudWatch/BigQuery). 90 days retention is fine; for longer retention we offer an add-on.

[06:00] Leah: on success criteria, we want: 1) scripted perf tests showing p95 under 400ms in staging, 2) security attestation (KMS + SSO), 3) runbook for failover.
[06:14] Maya: agreed. we'll propose a pilot with clear pass/fail.

[06:40] Jordan: any known gotchas about peering across regions? we are in us-east-1 for production but want the inference to be in us-east-2 for capacity reasons.
[06:53] Brian: cross-region peering introduces extra latency; we recommend co-locating for latency sensitive cases. if you must keep separate, we can benchmark and possibly use a nearby region or enable a lower-quant model variant to save hops.

[07:30] Sam: also — compliance asks about encryption in transit. do you support mTLS and client certs?
[07:40] Maya: yes, we support TLS with mTLS options for private deployments, and SNI-based routing. we'll capture details in the runbook.

[08:05] Priya: for the staging run, we can open a test subnet; what's the network footprint we need to provide?
[08:15] Brian: minimal: CIDR block, endpoint IPs for whitelisting, and a route table. we'll send a template.

[09:00] Leah: timing — we aim to be in limited beta in mid-october, is that realistic?
[09:10] Maya: yes with a focused pilot. recommended cadence: week 0 connectivity + access, week 1 perf bench, week 2 security checks and canary.

[09:40] Jordan: on perf bench, do you have a benchmark harness?
[09:45] Brian: yes, we'll provide a lightweight script that simulates your QPS and token lengths. there was a small typo in an earlier doc where our metrics were labeled p90 p95 swapped — sorry if that caused confusion.

[10:22] (crosstalk) Priya: can we also test key rotation?
[10:25] Sam: yeah rotation and key-policies are critical.
[10:30] Brian: we can simulate key rotation in staging; I recommend a dry-run where we rotate keys and validate decryption flows.

[11:05] Jordan: what about burst capacity, do you offer autoscaling?
[11:12] Maya: Redwood Dedicated/Dedicaed-like pools can autoscale; in Private we can configure burst capacity and warm pools to reduce cold-start impact. the policy is configurable in the console.
[11:25] Priya: console access - we'll need RBAC and SSO (SAML) configured for our tooling team.
[11:33] Elena: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC. we will collect the IdP metadata as part of access onboarding.

[12:05] Leah: any concerns about log PII? we process traces and sometimes the prompts contain sensitive tokens.
[12:15] Sam: we want redaction or no retention of raw prompt payloads by default.
[12:22] Maya: by default in private deployments logs can be routed to your S3 and we can disable retention on our side. we can also set masking rules; I'll add that as a configuration option in the runbook.

[13:30] (brief silence)
[13:45] Priya: does Redwood support inference quantization / lower precision models to save cost? we might want to trade a little accuracy for latency/cost.
[13:56] Brian: yes, we have quantized model variants and can recommend profiles based on your evals. note quality regression monitoring is part of the Optimize tool — we can run a couple eval sets during pilot.

[15:00] Jordan: ok, governance — who at Redwood will be our day-to-day?
[15:06] Elena: I'll be your CSM for the onboarding, Maya is AE, Brian is SE for technical. We'll loop in product for anything model-specific.

[15:40] Leah: can we see the security whitepaper and SOC attestation?
[15:46] Maya: yes we'll send the security pack and a short compliance FAQ.

[16:05] (timestamp jump, a section later in call for technical deep-dive)
[16:12] Brian: quick topology sketch: we'll request a peered subnet; Redwood side needs an app-subnet and a control-plane endpoint whitelisted. keep NAT to a minimum. We'll provide CIDR templates and terraform fragments.
[16:35] Priya: terraform fragments are helpful — we use IaC heavily.
[16:40] Brian: great, we'll attach them to the runbook.

[18:00] Sam: any latency SLA you commit to for private deployments?
[18:07] Maya: for dedicated pools we have SLA targets on availability and throughput; for latency we provide performance profiles and can commit to targets in a reserved capacity contract. public-hosted has different guarantees. We'll draft suggested SLO language for the POC.

[19:20] Jordan: let's surface the top 3 risks now — I'll say 1) cross-region peering and latency 2) KMS edge-cases during rotation 3) RBAC/SSO provisioning complexity.
[19:35] Maya: agree. we can mitigate 1) by co-locating or benchmarking nearby region; 2) we'll do a rotation dry-run in staging; 3) we'll provide a SCIM SAML runbook and support a provisioning call.

[20:10] Leah: questions from our execs sometimes ask for a rollback/playbook for when latency breaches happen. do you have a failover option?
[20:22] Brian: yes, we can configure automatic fallback to a cheaper but compatible model or route to hosted fallback endpoints; that'll be in the runbook. for critical alerting you can pin to a low-latency model variant.

[21:05] (Elena enters next steps)
[21:10] Elena: recap — Runbook + terraform templates from Redwood, whitelist IPs and test dataset from Tileridge, schedule dry-run, and benchmark script. Any additions?
[21:24] Priya: include expected observability hooks and span ids for correlating traces.
[21:31] Brian: will do, we'll include trace headers and sample trace output.

[22:00] Maya: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the dry-run and attach the security pack.
[22:07] Jordan: perfect. thanks.

[22:45] (wrap up)
[22:50] Leah: thanks all — quick call but very useful.
[22:55] Sam: appreciate the clarity, look forward to the runbook.

[23:10] Maya: one more thing — there was a question about costs; I'll have a rough TCO for the pilot in the follow up email.
[23:20] Jordan: ok thanks everyone.

(There are a few short sections with slight mis-transcriptions: “Redwood Privat” instead of Private; small overlapping talk when Priya and Sam discussed rotation.)

Final recap (verbatim from call):
- Pilot scope: Staging VPC peering -> perf bench -> security dry-run -> canary
- Success: p95 < 400ms in staging under representative traffic, KMS + audit integrated, SSO + RBAC validated
- Risks: cross-region latency, KMS rotation edge cases, RBAC provisioning delays

Explicit next steps:
1) Maya to send VPC runbook, terraform sample, and security pack by 2027-09-14.
2) Priya to return whitelist IPs and provide sample telemetry/prompts by 2027-09-15.
3) Brian and Jordan to schedule a 1-hour dry-run week of 2027-09-20 and prepare benchmark script by 2027-09-17.
4) Sam to share audit event schema and KMS requirements by 2027-09-16.

Links mentioned:
